questions.q: What is the difference between a proper fraction and an improper fraction?
questions.a: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than the denominator, while an improper fraction has a numerator equal to or greater than the denominator. A student who says "proper is always smaller" may not realize that improper fractions can also represent values equal to 1 (like 4/4).

questions.q: Can a mixed number ever be a proper fraction? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, a mixed number consists of a whole number plus a proper fraction, meaning its total value is always greater than 1. Answering "yes" shows confusion between the "fractional part" of the mixed number and the mixed number as a whole.

questions.q: If you have 1 3/4 kg of rice, why is this equivalent to 7/4 kg?
questions.a: Each 1 whole contains 4/4, so 1 3/4 is (4/4 + 3/4) = 7/4. A wrong answer suggests the student added the whole number to the numerator (1+3=4) instead of converting the whole into the fractional unit.

questions.q: Which is greater: 5/4 or 1 1/4? Justify your choice.
questions.a: They are equal. 1 1/4 means 1 + 1/4, which is 4/4 + 1/4 = 5/4. Answering that one is greater suggests the student sees different notation as proof of a different value.

questions.q: Create a scenario involving 2 whole chikkis and 1/3 of another chikki. How would you write this as both an improper fraction and a mixed number?
questions.a: The mixed number is 2 1/3. The improper fraction is 7/3. A poor answer fails to realize that 2 wholes contain 6/3, leading to the total of 7/3.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A Proper fraction has a numerator smaller than the denominator (value < 1), an Improper fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to the denominator (value ≥ 1), and a Mixed number ______ an improper fraction as a whole number combined with a proper fraction.
Fill in the blank: You might say each gets "one and two-thirds" (a mixed number) or "five-thirds" (an ______ fraction).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to classify any given fraction as proper, improper, or mixed, and convert between improper fractions and mixed numbers with 100% accuracy.
